prior_review_decision: REJECT (PR #5698 exact head 351e58de1980a9d32c10ccefde8accc4cb48004e, frozen manifest blob 718ddbd91a5c39730c9942e5857325c6727e5b2c): (P1) management_read_models/service.py:2423-2428 get_context_rollbacks unconditionally returned status=ok/source_kind=live after any non-raising read, discarding the returned rollback owner's real status and provenance; with a rollback record explicitly status=unavailable/source_kind=unavailable/owner=rollback-owner/degradation_reason=rollback owner offline, both trading_pulse and cockpit context chains reported ok and omitted the failed owner. (P1) main.py:15143-15151 _mgmt_nl_surface_owner_observation reconstructed a partial untyped dict and dropped source_version, observed_at, freshness_seconds and correlation_id from incident/approval/sentinel surface observations, and ignored canonical source_kind/degradation_reason keys on the surface. Earlier prior_head 1feba567813892e507f4cfda6a65348cb330779b was rejected for: (P1) main.py:15170-15213 reads alerts/inbox/anomalies payloads but discards their meta.surfaces; the cockpit merge included only runtime and telemetry, so with healthy runtime/telemetry and incident_feed, approval_queue, or sentinel_findings explicitly unavailable, management_cockpit reported ok and omitted the failed owner and reason. (P1) main.py:6315-6326 still called bare monitoring/rollback reads inside the shared pulse helper; if either raised after successful runtime and telemetry reads, main.py:15237-15238 returned only status=unavailable/source=error and discarded both collected owners and the failure reason. Earlier prior_head 77526b3c525d9908b3a7e7e823b1e8221285c260 was rejected for: (P1) main.py:15179-15188 invokes _mgmt_nl_trading_pulse_snippet -> _mgmt_nl_scoped_runtime_rows -> _project_operator_runtime_state_row, which still called bare read_store.get_telemetry_summary directly instead of a purpose-built owner accessor; with a healthy runtime binding and a telemetry record explicitly status=unavailable/degradation_reason=telemetry owner offline, management_trading_pulse reported status=ok and dropped all telemetry owner provenance. (P1) if that bare telemetry read raised, main.py:15190-15191 discarded even the already-collected runtime owner observation and returned only status=unavailable/source=error with no typed owner or degradation reason. Earlier prior_head 8d5b06ba7d0cd7d6ce9f375aeed66bbff93c88c8 was rejected for: (P1) service.py:2171-2190 still selected max(provenance_records) as the single observation for the entire list; with two same-tenant unavailable owners carrying distinct owner/source_version/correlation_id and the same degradation_reason, portfolio context completely omitted the second owner's identity/version/correlation, and reversing row order changed which unavailable owner disappeared. Joining reason strings did not preserve per-owner provenance, and mixed degraded/unavailable owners lost provenance too. Earlier prior_head 1e8192a3ada9ffdbefe4f332d2a73ad35cff88fe was rejected for: (P1) main.py:15186 forced management_trading_pulse.status=ok whenever runtime_bindings was nonempty, even when its owner_observation explicitly reported unavailable or degraded. (P1) service.py:2095-2098 and 2156-2170 selected the first provenance-bearing record as the observation for the entire list; a same-tenant healthy owner row followed by an unavailable owner row made portfolio_book report ok and completely omitted the later owner's degradation/provenance from the context -- reversing row order changed reported availability. Earlier prior_head 8e79502c5c27ab3dc182a8f7a1f454dd18781a6d was rejected for: (P1) a nonempty owner projection whose record itself carried status=unavailable/source_kind=unavailable/degradation_reason=owner offline was promoted to status=ok and lost its degradation_reason in both _typed_context_list and get_context_telemetry_summary, because both always forced status=ok (or the empty-vs-nonempty-derived status) once any provenance record was found, ignoring the record's own status/degradation_reason fields. (P1) _context_observation fabricated observed_at=now()/freshness_seconds=0 whenever a caller (including backfill records with observed_at=None, no-provenance records, and unavailable reads) passed observed_at=None, instead of preserving unknown observation time/freshness as null. (P2) when the real RuntimePort provider answered a status probe successfully and then failed on the actual read (error swallowed inside the port, returning an empty list), _typed_context_list's no-provenance fallback returned status=degraded/source_kind=live/degradation_reason=None/freshness=0, reading as a healthy live observation instead of an explained degradation tied to that read. Earlier prior_head ddae71d1ce4d48fbfdc3e5818eebefcb1f0c06b6 was rejected for: (P1) main.py built observations before tenant filtering and service.py selected the first global record's provenance, so a tenant-a context could carry tenant-b owner/source_version/correlation_id even at runtime_count=0. (P1) service.py's get_context_telemetry_summary overwrote successful telemetry backfill/replay provenance with owner=runtime_id, source_kind=live, source_version/correlation_id=None, observed_at=now, freshness=0. (P1) service.py probed domain surface status separately before the actual list read; a provider that answered the probe successfully and then failed on the real read (error swallowed inside the port) was reported as an empty ok/live row instead of failing closed. (P1) main.py ignored non-telemetry owner failures when aggregating portfolio_book/persona_fleet status (e.g. runtime owner raising while pools/personas existed still reported status=ok).

implementation.summary: Management AI context collection (_mgmt_nl_collect_context in main.py) previously reached the Management domain by calling the module-global ReadSurfacePorts object (read_store.list_runtime_bindings/list_capital_pools/list_incidents/list_evolution_decisions/get_telemetry_summary) directly -- generic store access bypassing the purpose-built ManagementService. Replaced every such call with new purpose-built ManagementService context accessors (get_context_runtime_bindings, get_context_capital_pools, get_context_incidents, get_context_evolution_decisions, get_context_telemetry_summary), instantiated once as module-level _management_ai_context_service bound to the same app_deps.read_surface used by the Management read-model routers. Each accessor returns (items, ManagementObservation) instead of a bare list: an unavailable or failing domain now returns an explicit typed degraded row (source_kind=unavailable, degradation_reason set) rather than an ad hoc {"status": "unavailable"} dict or a silently empty list, and the row is threaded into the NL context surfaces payload (owner_observation / owner_observations) so unavailable owners are never silently omitted.
implementation.post_reject_fix_summary: Addressed the three P1 defects from the first independent reject: (1) _typed_context_list now resolves each subject's real domain surface status via ReadSurfacePorts.get_surface_status() (persona_capital_runtime.runtime/capital/evolution.surfaces.evolution_decisions) before trusting a non-raising empty list; an unconfigured/provider-failed owner is reported status=unavailable even though the underlying port call itself did not raise (subjects with no such upstream signal, e.g. incidents, keep the prior try/except-based inference, documented in _DOMAIN_SURFACE_STATUS_PATH). (2) _context_observation is now built through the previously-unused ManagementObservation pydantic model (model_dump()) instead of a hand-rolled dict, and _typed_context_list inspects returned records for real owner/source_kind/source_version/observed_at/correlation_id provenance (via _record_provenance) and preserves it verbatim -- including computing freshness_seconds from the real observed_at instead of always stamping now()/freshness=0 or promoting replay/backfill to live. (3) get_context_telemetry_summary now returns (summary, ManagementObservation) instead of swallowing exceptions into None; _mgmt_nl_collect_context's portfolio branch aggregates every telemetry observation into owner_observations and sets portfolio_book status=degraded whenever any telemetry read failed, instead of staying ok solely because pools/runtime bindings existed.
implementation.second_post_reject_fix_summary: Addressed the four P1 defects from the second independent reject: (1) _typed_context_list now accepts an optional record_filter callable; _mgmt_nl_collect_context passes a tenant-scoping filter (built from the existing _mgmt_nl_filter_tenant_records) into every get_context_runtime_bindings/get_context_capital_pools/get_context_incidents/get_context_evolution_decisions call across the cockpit, trading_pulse, portfolio, and persona_fleet branches, so unauthorized-tenant records are dropped before _record_provenance ever inspects them -- a tenant-a call can no longer surface a tenant-b owner/source_version/correlation_id even when its own scoped record count is zero. (2) get_context_telemetry_summary now runs the same _record_provenance derivation used for list-shaped subjects against the returned summary dict and preserves its real owner/source_kind/source_version/observed_at/correlation_id instead of always stamping runtime_id/live/now/freshness=0. (3) _typed_context_list no longer trusts a pre-read domain_status probe to justify status=ok when the actual read comes back empty (a flaky/failing provider can answer the probe successfully and then fail on the real read, with the port swallowing the error into an empty list); status is now derived from the real read outcome -- non-empty is ok, empty fails closed to unavailable (domain_status said so) or degraded (ambiguous/no signal). (4) main.py's portfolio_book and persona_fleet status now aggregate every contributing owner_observation status (pools/runtime/telemetry for portfolio; runtime/incidents/evolution_decisions for persona_fleet) instead of only checking telemetry or record presence, so a runtime-owner failure can no longer be masked by a coexisting pool/persona success.
implementation.third_post_reject_fix_summary: Addressed the three defects from the third independent reject (P1, P1, P2), all in service.py: (1) _context_observation no longer fabricates observed_at/freshness_seconds when observed_at is None -- it only derives freshness from an observed_at that was actually supplied, otherwise both stay null, regardless of source_kind or caller (backfill records, no-provenance records, and unavailable reads all now preserve unknown observation time instead of stamping now()/freshness=0). (2) _typed_context_list's and get_context_telemetry_summary's provenance-found branch now uses the record's own status (falling back to the count-derived status only when the record has none) and threads the record's own degradation_reason through, instead of always forcing status=ok merely because a provenance-bearing record was present -- an owner-reported unavailable/degraded record is preserved verbatim, never promoted to ok. (3) _typed_context_list's no-provenance fallback now branches on the computed status: only a genuinely ok (non-empty, provenance-less) read still reports source_kind=live with no degradation_reason; a degraded/unavailable outcome (e.g. a status probe that reported healthy immediately before the real read silently returned nothing) now reports source_kind=unavailable with an explicit degradation_reason instead of a bare live/None/freshness=0 triple that reads as healthy.
implementation.fourth_post_reject_fix_summary: Addressed the two P1 defects from the fourth independent reject: (1) main.py's trading_pulse branch no longer overrides management_trading_pulse.status to 'ok' whenever runtime_bindings is nonempty; it now always uses runtime_bindings_obs['status'] verbatim, so an owner_observation that reports unavailable/degraded is preserved through to the surface status instead of being masked by nonemptiness alone. (2) service.py's _record_provenance now returns every provenance-bearing record instead of only the first one, and _typed_context_list's provenance branch aggregates across all of them: the worst-ranked status (unavailable > degraded > ok) wins independent of record order, and every non-ok record's degradation_reason is joined into the resulting observation, so a same-tenant healthy owner row followed (or preceded) by an unavailable owner row can no longer make the aggregate report ok or drop the later owner's degradation/provenance -- reversing row order no longer changes reported availability. get_context_telemetry_summary's single-record call site was updated to take the first (only) entry from the now-list-returning _record_provenance.
implementation.fifth_post_reject_fix_summary: Addressed the single P1 defect from the fifth independent reject, all in service.py/models.py: _typed_context_list's provenance branch aggregated every contributing provenance-bearing record into one worst-status winner via max(), which silently discarded every other same-tenant owner's identity/version/correlation/observed_at even when it was the only remaining evidence of a second unavailable owner. ManagementObservation now carries a new contributing_observations: List[Dict] field (models.py), and _typed_context_list builds one typed observation per provenance-bearing record (subject_id derived from the record's own runtime_id/binding_id/pool_id/decision_id/incident_id/id via the new _record_subject_id helper) and attaches the full list to the aggregate observation's contributing_observations. The aggregate's top-level scalar fields (owner/source_kind/source_version/observed_at/correlation_id/status) still report the worst-ranked winner unchanged, preserving every existing caller and test that reads those fields directly; every contributing owner's full provenance now also survives inside contributing_observations regardless of row order or mixed degraded/unavailable statuses, and is threaded into every context surface (owner_observation/owner_observations) unchanged because those surfaces already embed the full aggregate observation object.
implementation.eighth_post_reject_fix_summary: Addressed the two P1 defects from the eighth independent reject: (1) service.py's get_context_rollbacks previously returned rollbacks with a hardcoded status=ok/source_kind=live observation regardless of what the read itself carried; it now runs the same provenance aggregation used by _typed_context_list -- _record_provenance/worst-status-wins/contributing_observations -- against the returned rollback rows, so a rollback record that itself reports status=unavailable/owner/source_version/observed_at/correlation_id/degradation_reason is preserved and aggregated into the rollback_observation instead of being discarded after a non-raising read. (2) main.py's _mgmt_nl_surface_owner_observation now reads source_version, observed_at, freshness_seconds and correlation_id directly off the surface dict (in addition to the existing status/owner) and prefers a surface's own source_kind/degradation_reason keys over the previous source/message-only fallback, so every incident_feed/approval_queue/sentinel_findings surface's full provenance survives cockpit owner-observation conversion instead of being reconstructed as a partial untyped dict.
implementation.row_shape_added: ManagementObservation pydantic model added to management_read_models/models.py (subject_type, subject_id, status, owner, source_kind: live|replayed|backfill|unavailable, source_version, observed_at, freshness_seconds, degradation_reason, correlation_id, contributing_observations: List[Dict] default []) per SD sec7.1; now constructed directly by service.py instead of being unused.
implementation.sixth_post_reject_fix_summary: Addressed the two P1 defects from the sixth independent reject, both in main.py: the real trading-pulse/cockpit helper path (_mgmt_nl_trading_pulse_snippet -> _mgmt_nl_scoped_runtime_rows -> _project_operator_runtime_state_row) still called bare read_store.get_telemetry_summary(runtime_id) instead of the purpose-built ManagementService.get_context_telemetry_summary accessor already used by the portfolio/persona_fleet branches. (1) _project_operator_runtime_state_row now routes its non-prefetched telemetry read through _management_ai_context_service.get_context_telemetry_summary(runtime_id) and threads the returned ManagementObservation onto the row as telemetry_observation; this accessor never raises (a read failure is reported as a typed unavailable observation instead of propagating), which also eliminates the second defect (a raising telemetry read no longer discards the already-collected runtime owner observation, because the read can no longer raise). (2) _mgmt_nl_trading_pulse_snippet now collects every row's telemetry_observation into a new telemetry_observations list on its return value, and a new _mgmt_nl_merge_owner_observations helper aggregates the runtime_bindings owner observation with every contributing telemetry observation into one worst-status-wins ManagementObservation-shaped dict (status/degradation_reason taken from the worst-ranked contributor, every contributor's provenance preserved verbatim in contributing_observations) -- both the management_cockpit and management_trading_pulse surfaces now report this merged observation instead of runtime_bindings_obs alone, so a telemetry owner explicitly reporting unavailable can no longer be masked by a healthy runtime binding, and its owner/degradation_reason/correlation_id survive into the surface regardless of whether the read raised.
implementation.seventh_post_reject_fix_summary: Addressed the two P1 defects from the seventh independent reject, both in main.py/service.py: (1) _mgmt_nl_collect_context's cockpit branch built alerts_payload/human_inbox_payload/anomalies_payload but only ever passed runtime_bindings_obs and trading_pulse telemetry observations into _mgmt_nl_merge_owner_observations -- every surface entry inside each payload's meta.surfaces (e.g. incident_feed, approval_queue, sentinel_findings) was read for record filtering but never converted into an owner observation, so an unavailable non-runtime surface could not affect management_cockpit's merged status. A new _mgmt_nl_surface_owner_observation helper converts any dataset/aggregate surface-status dict into the same observation shape as a typed context-service observation, and a new _mgmt_nl_payload_surface_observations helper turns every entry in a payload's meta.surfaces into one such observation; the cockpit branch now merges these alongside runtime_bindings_obs and the trading-pulse telemetry observations, so every contributing cockpit surface's real availability is preserved regardless of which one fails. (2) _project_operator_runtime_state_row called read_store.get_paper_runtime_monitoring_session and read_store.get_rollbacks bare (unlike the already-fixed telemetry read); a raised exception from either propagated up through _mgmt_nl_scoped_runtime_rows/_mgmt_nl_trading_pulse_snippet into _mgmt_nl_collect_context's try/except, which discarded every already-collected owner observation (runtime, telemetry) and returned a bare status=unavailable/source=error with no owner or reason. Two new typed accessors, ManagementService.get_context_monitoring_session and ManagementService.get_context_rollbacks (service.py), mirror get_context_telemetry_summary's never-raises contract; _project_operator_runtime_state_row now routes both reads through them and threads the resulting observations onto the row as monitoring_observation/rollback_observation, and _mgmt_nl_trading_pulse_snippet folds them into the same telemetry_observations list consumed by both the cockpit and trading_pulse merges, so a monitoring/rollback read failure can no longer discard the runtime/telemetry owners already collected for that surface.
